source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Astika sub-parva, adhyayas 47–48 (Janamejaya learns how his father died and vows the sarpa-satra; the builder's warning; the priests in black; the serpents fall into the fire; Takshaka flees to Indra)
structure: Every episode: RECAP (≈3 s; KIT.series.recapStrip) → HOOK (one question, Sauti at the Naimisha fire; the episode title follows it: KIT.series.episodeTitle) → STORY → NEXT (a cliffhanger line, then the teaser card: KIT.series.nextTeaser).

voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`). captionY (px or "high") lifts the caption above low action.

lines.text: Takshaka killed King Parikshit with his venom.
lines.note: RECAP. Episode 7's key image as a memory: the serpent king rising over the king in the pavilion, the venom-fire. beats = 'killed', 'venom'

lines.speaker: sauti
lines.note: HOOK (Sauti at the Naimisha fire). The fire leaps; in its smoke the young king's crowned profile, then a ring of falling serpents. beats = 'Janamejaya', 'revenge'; the title shows in the post

lines.text: His ministers told young Janamejaya how his father died.
lines.note: STORY 1. The court at Hastinapura (EP6.court, saffron lamplight): the young king enthroned, old ministers bowing before him; in the lamp smoke between them a memory: the pillar, the green hood. beats = 'ministers', 'Janamejaya', 'died'

lines.speaker: janamejaya
lines.text: I will burn Takshaka and all his kind in the fire!
lines.say: I will burn Takshaka… [p:100] and all his kind in the fire!
lines.note: STORY 2 (Janamejaya speaks). He rises from the throne, wrath, his hand raised; the lamps flare. beats = 'burn', 'Takshaka', 'fire'

lines.text: As the ground was measured, a builder foretold: a brahmin would stop this rite.
lines.say: As the ground was measured, [p:80] a builder foretold: [p:150] a brahmin would stop this rite.
lines.note: STORY 3. NEW PLACE: the sacrifice ground at dawn (grey-rose light, cords and pegs). A builder with a measuring cord kneels at the boundary; he looks up and raises a warning finger; a small boy's shadow (Astika, foreshadowed) falls across the cord. beats = 'measured', 'builder', 'brahmin'

lines.text: Priests in black, their eyes red with smoke, called the serpents by name.
lines.say: Priests in black, [p:80] their eyes red with smoke, [p:100] called the serpents by name.
lines.note: STORY 4. The sarpa-satra: a vast smoky crimson enclosure, the great fire in its altar, four priests in black robes around it pouring ghee and chanting, their eyes glowing red; the king offers with the ladle. beats = 'black', 'smoke', 'serpents' (the first hoods appear in the clouds)

lines.text: And serpents of every size and colour fell into the fire.
lines.note: STORY 5. Looking up: serpents of every size and colour (small green, banded gold, red, great black-hooded), drawn helplessly down through the smoke in spirals and into the fire: mural shapes, no gore; each becomes a burst of sparks. beats = 'serpents', 'size', 'fire'

lines.text: Bound by the mantras, not one could escape.
lines.say: Bound by the mantras… [p:80] not one could escape.
lines.note: STORY 5b. Close on the fire: a great hooded serpent strains against the pull, coils thrashing, but gold mantra-light binds it and draws it down into the flames (a burst of sparks; mural, no gore). beats = 'mantras' (gold bands), 'one', 'escape'

lines.text: Takshaka fled to Indra, king of the gods.
lines.note: STORY 6. NEW PLACE: Indra's heaven, white-gold clouds and a pale palace; Takshaka rises up through the clouds, coiling, afraid, before Indra on his throne with the vajra. beats = 'Takshaka', 'Indra' (name label)

lines.speaker: indra
lines.text: Stay with me, Takshaka. You are safe.
lines.say: Stay with me, Takshaka. [p:150] You are safe.
lines.note: STORY 7 (Indra speaks). He raises his hand in protection; the vajra glows; Takshaka coils at his feet. beats = 'Stay', 'safe'

lines.text: Why were the serpents doomed? Because their own mother cursed them.
lines.say: Why were the serpents doomed? [p:200] Because their own mother… cursed them.
lines.note: NEXT 1. Back at the sacrifice, the fire roars; in its smoke the shape of a woman, crowned, her hand raised in a curse over a nest of serpent eggs. beats = 'doomed', 'own', 'cursed'
the teaser card, with a glimpse of episode 9: Kashyapa's hermitage, two sisters, a thousand eggs and two
